targets.authors: Dufour V., Sterck E. H. M.
targets.title: Chimpanzees fail to plan in an exchange task but succeed in a tool-using procedure.
targets.evidence_quote: In order to discern whether the ability for deferred exchange with humans is outside the cognitive scope of great apes, the current study aimed to replicate the main experiment of Dufour and Sterck (2008) with subjects with everyday experience of direct exchange with humans.
targets.outcome_quote: The goal was to discern whether great apes indeed are incapable of using an arbitrary but reinforced object to make exchanges for food with humans after a considerable delay, as has been suggested by the results in Dufour and Sterck (2008). Our results show, contrary to the previous study that it is within the abilities of both chimpanzees and orangutans.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The target reported failure in deferred exchange; this study explicitly contradicts that finding by demonstrating deferred exchange. Positive performance therefore represents failure to replicate the original negative finding. Osvath and Osvath supplied a selection procedure rather than a separate finding targeted here.

reasoning: Two experiments with a new ape sample retest the deferred-exchange result of Dufour and Sterck, with both close and modified selection procedures.
